slides.teacher_cue: What sound?
slides.expected_response: Students produce /s/ quickly and cleanly.
slides.correction_move: Model /s/, students repeat three times, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /sh/ drift and delayed retrieval.

slides.teacher_cue: What sound?
slides.expected_response: Students produce /æ/ quickly and cleanly.
slides.correction_move: Model /æ/, students repeat three times, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for uncertain retrieval and drifting vowel quality.

slides.teacher_cue: What sound?
slides.expected_response: Students produce /t/ quickly and cleanly.
slides.correction_move: Model /t/, students repeat three times, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for weak release or delayed retrieval.

slides.teacher_cue: Play sat once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write sat accurately.
slides.correction_move: Replay sat once, then segment /s/ /æ/ /t/ orally before rechecking.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can still hold the full word from sound to print.

slides.teacher_cue: Play at once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write at accurately.
slides.correction_move: Replay at once, then segment /æ/ /t/ orally before rechecking.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students add an extra sound before or after the word.

slides.teacher_cue: Play as once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write as accurately.
slides.correction_move: Replay as once, then segment /æ/ /s/ orally before rechecking.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students hear the final /s/ clearly in a short word.

slides.teacher_cue: New sound today. Lips slightly spread, tongue mid-high, brief. Not a long eeee — just a quick i.
slides.expected_response: Students produce short /ɪ/ cleanly without stretching or tensing it.
slides.correction_move: Model a short relaxed /ɪ/, contrast it with a sustained /iː/, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for tense overlong vowel production — Korean learners may produce /iː/ instead of /ɪ/.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the new focus, then connect i to one strong word from today.
slides.expected_response: Students say i clearly and connect it to a lesson word.
slides.correction_move: Model the focus once, then have students echo and use it in a known word.
slides.observation_note: Listen for whether students can carry the focus from isolation into a real word.

slides.teacher_cue: Sight word — underlined. Say it as a whole unit. Uses /aɪ/ diphthong — not taught until Lesson 34. Learn as a whole unit. Use it in a short oral sentence, then reveal.
slides.expected_response: Students say I orally and recognise it as a whole-unit sight word.
slides.correction_move: Model I in a sentence, point to the underline, repeat chorally.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students try to blend I. Redirect — sight word, say it whole.

slides.teacher_cue: Sight word — underlined. Say it as a whole unit. Uses voiced /ð/ — not taught until Lesson 23. Learn as a whole unit. Use it in a short oral sentence, then reveal.
slides.expected_response: Students say the orally and recognise it as a whole-unit sight word.
slides.correction_move: Model the in a sentence, point to the underline, repeat chorally.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students try to blend the. Redirect — sight word, say it whole.

slides.teacher_cue: Sight word — underlined. Say it as a whole unit. Uses schwa /ə/ — not formally taught. Learn as a whole unit. Use it in a short oral sentence, then reveal.
slides.expected_response: Students say a orally and recognise it as a whole-unit sight word.
slides.correction_move: Model a in a sentence, point to the underline, repeat chorally.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students try to blend a. Redirect — sight word, say it whole.

slides.teacher_cue: Model the action, say the word, then reveal print. All three sounds are taught.
slides.expected_response: Students say sit orally, connect it to the action, then blend the three sounds on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model the action again, say sit slowly, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students hold the short /ɪ/ in the middle and do not stretch it to /iː/.

slides.teacher_cue: Point to an object and say it orally, then reveal print. Use in a short oral sentence: I sat. It sat.
slides.expected_response: Students say it orally in context and recognise it as a high-frequency word.
slides.correction_move: Model it in a short oral sentence, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students treat it as a useful word in context, not just isolated sounds.

slides.teacher_cue: Model its orally with a possessive gesture, then reveal print and blend all three sounds.
slides.expected_response: Students say its orally with a sense of ownership meaning, then blend the three sounds on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model its with a clear gesture, say it again slowly, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students preserve the final /s/ both orally and when blending.

slides.teacher_cue: Use is orally in a short sentence — I sat. It is. Then reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say is orally in context before seeing it in print.
slides.correction_move: Model is in a short oral sentence, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can use is orally before print exposure. Note: s here makes /z/ — flag this if students query it.

slides.teacher_cue: Read it, track the parts, and confirm that every part fits the taught pool for i.
slides.expected_response: Students read the word accurately and explain why it is safe to read.
slides.correction_move: Tap each sound or chunk, blend, then reread smoothly.
slides.observation_note: Use this as confidence-building cumulative review, not as a surprise challenge.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build left to right. The new vowel goes in the middle.
slides.expected_response: Students build sit correctly: s | i | t.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of sit, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students place the new short i in the middle slot without hesitation.

slides.teacher_cue: Build the word from left to right.
slides.expected_response: Students build it correctly: i | t.
slides.correction_move: Say it orally, isolate each sound, then rebuild.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can map a short two-sound word accurately without reversing.

slides.teacher_cue: Build the word and keep all three sounds — including the final one.
slides.expected_response: Students build its correctly: i | t | s.
slides.correction_move: Say its orally, segment all three sounds, then rebuild from the start.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students preserve the final /s/ and do not stop at i | t.

content_payload.prompt_text: Build the i word, read it, then rebuild it without help.

slides.teacher_cue: Build the i word once, read it, clear it, then rebuild it without help.
slides.expected_response: Students build, read, clear, and rebuild accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model one build slowly, then have students repeat with less support.
slides.observation_note: Watch for whether students are mapping parts to print or only recalling the shape.

slides.teacher_cue: Track left to right and read the full sentence. I is a sight word — say it as a whole unit.
slides.expected_response: Students read "I sit." accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model the sentence once, then return to one-to-one word tracking.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students hold the short /ɪ/ inside a simple sentence and do not stretch it.

slides.teacher_cue: Track left to right. Both words are decodable — blend through each one.
slides.expected_response: Students read "It sat." accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model the sentence once, then return to one-to-one tracking.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can keep it and sat distinct — both use known phonemes but different vowels.

content_payload.text_content:
I sit.
It sat.
I sat.

slides.teacher_cue: Read all three sentences left to right. Gesture to each subject as you go — I, then it, then I again. Ask: what did each one do? This previews the full reader in Block 07.
slides.expected_response:
Students read "I sit.
It sat.
I sat." accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model each sentence once, name the subject, then echo-read together before moving on.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students read I sat. correctly — same sentence as G1-L1, now part of a three-sentence scene. Watch for vowel drift in all three sit/sat occurrences.

content_payload.text_content:
I sit.
It sat.
I sat.
content_payload.comprehension_prompt: What does this tell you about the lesson words? Say it back in your own words.

slides.teacher_cue: Read it smoothly, then explain the i idea in your own words.
slides.expected_response: Students read accurately and explain the meaning of the i sentence.
slides.correction_move: Reread in a phrase, then prompt for a brief retell or answer.
slides.observation_note: Push comprehension right after decoding so the focus does not stay mechanical.

content_payload.text_content:
I sit.
It sat.
I sat.
content_payload.comprehension_prompt: What did I do? What did it do? Point to the word that has the new sound.

slides.teacher_cue: Use the image to establish the scene before reading — who is I, what is it. Echo read each line, then read chorally with word tracking. After reading, ask the comprehension prompt.
slides.expected_response: Students read all three sentences accurately, hold the correct vowel in each word, and answer what each subject did.
slides.correction_move: Echo read line by line. For vowel errors, isolate the word, say it slowly, then reread the full sentence.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students track each word precisely and hold /ɪ/ in sit and /æ/ in sat across the full passage. The third sentence I sat. connects to G1-L1 — note if students show recall or hesitation.

content_payload.text_content:
I sit.
It sat.
I sat.
content_payload.comprehension_prompt: Reread smoothly. Point to one lesson word and use it in a new sentence.

slides.teacher_cue: Reread the full text for smoother phrasing. Then have students point to one lesson word and say a new sentence with it.
slides.expected_response: Students reread with smoother phrasing and produce one oral sentence using a lesson word.
slides.correction_move: Echo read one line at a time, then reread the full text and prompt one supported oral sentence.
slides.observation_note: Watch for improved fluency, accurate tracking, and whether students can transfer one lesson word into a new sentence.

content_payload.text_content:
I sit.
It sat.
I sat.
content_payload.comprehension_prompt: Reread the i text smoothly. Then tell one thing you noticed about the lesson words.

slides.teacher_cue: Read the i text again smoothly. Scoop the words into phrases and keep your voice steady.
slides.expected_response: Students reread with smoother phrasing and stronger fluency.
slides.correction_move: Model one line with phrasing, then have students echo and reread the whole text.
slides.observation_note: Listen for phrasing, expression, and control, not just speed.

slides.teacher_cue: Dictate sit once. Replay once only if needed. Students segment then write.
slides.expected_response: Students write sit accurately using the short i vowel.
slides.correction_move: Say sit again, segment /s/ /ɪ/ /t/ orally, then rewrite.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students encode the new /ɪ/ correctly and do not substitute a or e.

slides.teacher_cue: Dictate it once. Replay once only if needed. Students segment then write.
slides.expected_response: Students write it accurately as i | t.
slides.correction_move: Say it again, segment /ɪ/ /t/ orally, then rewrite.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can encode a short two-sound word without reversing or adding a letter.

slides.teacher_cue: Dictate its once. Replay once only if needed. Students segment then write.
slides.expected_response: Students write its accurately as i | t | s.
slides.correction_move: Say its again, segment /ɪ/ /t/ /s/ orally, then rewrite.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students preserve the final /s/ when encoding and do not stop at it.

content_payload.prompt_text: Write the i target from memory. Then read it back and check every part.

slides.teacher_cue: Write the i target carefully from memory, then read it back aloud and check every part.
slides.expected_response: Students write accurately and read back what they wrote.
slides.correction_move: Prompt students to say each sound or chunk as they check their writing.
slides.observation_note: The goal is accurate encoding plus immediate self-checking.

content_payload.support_text: What changed? Which sound is different?

slides.teacher_cue: Read sit and sat aloud. Ask: what changed in the middle?
slides.expected_response: Students identify that the vowel changed from /ɪ/ to /æ/ — one sound swap, different word.
slides.correction_move: Model both words, isolate the middle vowel in each, then ask again.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can hear and name that a single vowel change creates a completely different word.

content_payload.comprehension_prompt: Read the model sentence. Then say a new sentence with one lesson word.

slides.teacher_cue: Use the model sentence once, then ask students to say a new sentence that keeps one lesson word but changes the meaning.
slides.expected_response: Students read the model sentence and say one new oral sentence using a lesson word.
slides.correction_move: Model one new sentence aloud, then have students repeat and generate their own.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can hold the target pattern while generating a meaningful new sentence.

content_payload.comprehension_prompt: Say one sentence using i, then say a second sentence with one change.

slides.teacher_cue: Use i in one full sentence. Then change one part and say a second sentence.
slides.expected_response: Students produce one complete sentence and then extend or vary it.
slides.correction_move: Model one sentence, then prompt for a second sentence with one changed word or part.
slides.observation_note: Push for full oral language, not one-word answers.

content_payload.title: Close the Lesson

check_items.label: We have four sounds now: s, a, t, i. Which new sound did we learn today?
What did I do? What did it do? Point to the word that has the new sound.
Tell me one full sentence using I or the.

content_payload.notes_field: Keep the close brief, oral, and text-based.

slides.teacher_cue: Close with pattern recall, meaning from the reader, and one brief oral transfer sentence.
slides.expected_response: Students answer orally, refer back to the reader when needed, and produce one full sentence with lesson vocabulary.
slides.correction_move: Return to the reader, point to the relevant sentence, then model one full oral answer.
slides.observation_note: Watch for pattern recall, text-based answers, and whether the final oral sentence stays accurate and complete.

slides.teacher_cue: Show the sentence starter. Students write one full sentence that uses at least one lesson word from today.
slides.expected_response: Students write one complete sentence using at least one lesson word.
slides.correction_move: Model one short sentence aloud, then have students write their own version.
slides.observation_note: Watch for accurate spelling of lesson words and a complete sentence frame.

content_payload.support_text: Say one final strong sentence using today's i focus.

slides.teacher_cue: Give me one more full sentence or idea using today's i focus before we finish.
slides.expected_response: Students give one final complete sentence or idea connected to the lesson focus.
slides.correction_move: If needed, model the start of a sentence and have students finish it clearly.
slides.observation_note: End with a strong oral response so the lesson closes on language and meaning.
